questions.q: Suppose that the side lengths of a triangle are three consecutive integers and one of the angles is twice another. The number of such triangles is/are
questions.solution:
Let $\text{B} = 2\text{A}$ and $\text{B}\text{D}$ be the bisector of angle $\text{B}$, then

$\text{CD} = \dfrac{\text{ab}}{\text{a} + \text{c}} \text{$ and $} \text{AD} = \dfrac{\text{bc}}{\text{a} + \text{c}}$

Now,  $\Delta \text{ABC}$ and \Delta $\text{BDC}$ are similar, so

$\dfrac{\text{BC}}{\text{AC}} = \dfrac{\text{CD}}{\text{BC}} ⇒ {\text{a}}^{2} = \dfrac{\text{ab}}{\text{a} + \text{c}} \text{b} ⇒ {\text{b}}^{2} = \text{a} \left(\text{a}$ + $\text{c}\right)     ......(i)

Since, \text{b} > \text{a} ⇒$ Either $\text{b} = \text{a} +1$ or $\text{b} = \text{a} +2,$ if $\text{b} = \text{a} +$1,$ then [From Eq.(i)]

${$\left(\text{a} +1\right)$}^{2} = $\left(\text{a} + \text{c}\right) \text{a} ⇒ \text{c} =2 + \dfrac{1}{\text{a}}$

 
$\text{c} i$s integer $⇒ \text{a} =1, \text{b} =2, \text{c} =3$ but then, no triangle will form.
If $\text{b} = \text{a} +$2,$ then obviously \text{c} = \text{a} +1,$ and then, [from Eq. (i)]

${\left(\text{a}$ +2\right)$}^{2} = $$\text{a}$\left(2 $\text{a}$ +1\right)

$⇒ {$$\text{a}$$}^{2} - 3a - 4 = 0 $$\text{or}$$\text{a}$=$4$

$∴ $$\text{a}$$ =4, $$\text{b}$$ =6, $$\text{c}$$ =5$ is the only possible solution.

questions.q: The lengths of two adjacent sides of a cyclic quadrilateral are $2$ units and $5$ units and the angle between them is ${60}^{o}$. If the area of the quadrilateral is $4\sqrt{3}$& sq. units, then the perimeter of the quadrilateral is
questions.solution:
$cos ⁡ {60}^{o} = \dfrac{4 + 25 - c^{2}}{2.2. 5}$

$⇒ 10 = 29 - c^{2}$

$⇒ c^{2} = 19$

$⇒ c = \sqrt{19}$

Now,

$cos120° = \dfrac{a^{2} + b^{2} - c^{2}}{2ab}$

$⇒- \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{a^{2} + b^{2} - 19}{2ab}$

$⇒ a^{2} + b^{2} - 19 = - ab$

$⇒ a^{2} + b^{2} + ab = 19$

Area of quadrilateral $= \dfrac{1}{2} \times 2 \times 5sin ⁡ 60° + \dfrac{1}{2}absin ⁡ 120° = 4\sqrt{3}$

$⇒ \dfrac{5\sqrt{3}}{2} + \dfrac{ab\sqrt{3}}{4} = 4\sqrt{3}$

$⇒ \dfrac{ab}{4} = 4 - \dfrac{5}{2} = \dfrac{3}{2}$

$⇒ ab = 6$

$⇒ a^{2} + b^{2} = 13$

$⇒ a = 2, b = 3$

Perimeter

$= 2 + 5 + 2 + 3$

$= 12$

questions.q: Two sides of a triangle are given by the roots of the equation& $x^{2} - 2 \sqrt{3} \text{x} + 2 = 0$ and the angle between the sides is $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$. The perimeter of the triangle is
questions.solution:
Let the two sides $a$ and $b$ are the roots of the equation $x^{2} - 2 \sqrt{3} \text{x} + 2 = 0$.

$∴ \text{a} + \text{b} = 2 \sqrt{3}$ and $\text{ab} = 2$. Also, $∠ \text{C} = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$

Using cosine rule,

$\text{cosC} = \dfrac{a^{2} + b^{2} - c^{2}}{2\text{ab}} ⇒ \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{a^{2} + b^{2} - c^{2}}{2\text{ab}}$

$⇒ a^{2} + b^{2} - c^{2} = \text{ab} ⇒ {\left(\text{a} + \text{b}\right)}^{2} - c^{2} = 3 \text{ab}$

$⇒ {\left(2 \sqrt{3}\right)}^{2} - c^{2} = 3 \times 2 ⇒ \text{c} = \sqrt{6}$

$∴$ Perimeter $= \text{a} + \text{b} + \text{c} = 2\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{6}$ units
